dedupe_keys.name: radarsat constellation mission rcm image products and acquisition plans canadian space agency

description: The RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) is Canada's constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites. Its data serves Government of Canada needs first, but certain RCM image products are freely and openly available to users outside the government, subject to security, privacy and confidentiality exceptions. Public users register for an account on the Earth Observation Data Management System (EODMS) and can access, below 50 to 70 degrees latitude, products at 16 metre or coarser resolution over Canada's landmass and inland waters and international land, 100 metre products over world maritime areas and 50 metre or coarser products over the west Greenland maritime area. Organisations can apply to become vetted users with wider access after security screening; since April 2022 international entities can also apply. RCM standard coverage maps are issued every three months, and past and future acquisition plans are published on the Federal Geospatial Platform as vectors. Access for public users is free with registration; the Government of Canada terms apply and no separate licence is named on the page read. Caveats: not all products on the coverage maps are public, and vetting timelines are not guaranteed. Coverage is Canada and world maritime areas. It supports hazard exposure analysis such as flood and ice mapping near bridges, ports and northern roads; related records are the SANSA EO catalogue and the MYSA open data catalogue.
